activity_context.topic_title: Moments and Centers of Mass of Plane Laminas

feedback.problem: The lamina $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot [y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}-15{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[5{x}^{3}-3{x}^{5}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
